page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-96 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 360 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core execution, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls in the bottom 25 percent, reflecting the older architectural generation of the Intel Xeon processors in the N1 family. However, multi-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25 percent with a stress-ng multi-core score of 70594.44. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only cached and uncached operations scoring in the top 25 percent. Database operations, such as Redis SET, also perform strongly, achieving 62.03 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the n1-standard-96 is its lower single-threaded performance and lack of modern instruction sets like AVX-512 VNNI or AMX. This makes it less suitable for latency-sensitive single-threaded tasks or heavy real-time LLM text generation, where text generation speeds for medium models fall into the bottom 25 percent. However, its high core count and strong memory bandwidth make it highly cost-efficient for highly parallelized workloads. It is well-suited for multi-threaded batch processing, static web serving, software compilation, and database operations that can leverage its 96 dedicated vCPUs.
